ca_psychedelic_rock.blurb: Psychedelic Rock is a small bouldering area made up of twelve problems, tucked into the Split Rock zone of Cold Springs, a ridge-top climbing area above the Redwood Creek watershed in the mountains of northwest California. Problems run from V1 to V8, with most of them between V2 and V4, a pair at V6 and one high-end line, so intermediate boulderers will find the most to do. It is reached from the same main parking area as the neighbouring Spire and Dome, a short stroll through the woods. Development in the wider area is still ongoing, and there are plenty of unmarked trails around it.

ca_sw_face_right_monkey_business_wall.blurb: This is the right-hand stretch of the southwest face of Little Hunk, in the Echo Rock area of Joshua Tree National Park. It is mostly a traditional wall: ten of its twelve routes need gear, with one bolted line and one top-rope. Grades start at 5.7 and top out around 5.11, with about half of the routes at 5.10, so moderate leaders and stronger climbers both have options. Compared with the slabbier sections of the face to its left, this wall offers crack and face climbing, and it is the most visited stretch of the face. The block known as The Chair sits on top of the wall.
ca_sw_face_right_monkey_business_wall.parking_note: Leave the car in the large gravel lot beside Echo Tee.
ca_sw_face_right_monkey_business_wall.approach: From the lot, follow the signed trail east beyond the southern end of Echo Rock, then work around the south side of the formations to reach the wall. Allow roughly 10 to 15 minutes.

ca_potrero_john.blurb: Potrero John is a short cliff beside Highway 33 north of Ojai, about a quarter mile up the road from the Black Wall in Sespe Gorge. It is mainly a sport crag: eight bolted lines, two easy gear routes and a couple of V2 boulder problems. Most of the bolted routes sit around 5.10, with a few 5.8 and 5.9 lines to warm up on, and the style is delicate, technical face climbing on short routes. Later retro-bolting with bigger bolts and better anchors made it far friendlier to moderate climbers. The way in is a short descent down the hillside and across the creek.

ca_tunnel_crag.blurb: Tunnel Crag is a small sport crag high in the Angeles National Forest, at roughly 7,000 feet, found by driving the Angeles Crest Highway through its tunnels toward Islip Saddle. Twelve bolted routes run from 5.9 to low 5.11, with about half of them around 5.10 and four at 5.9, so newer leaders have something to try. Longer lines reach about 160 feet. Most routes face east, southeast or southwest and catch sun for much of the day in season. The rock quality is mixed, with loose stone in places, so a helmet is wise. Bring about a dozen quickdraws and your own water.

ca_visions_wall.blurb: Visions Wall is a slightly overhanging to vertical face in the Trinity Arêtes of Trinity County, northwest California, just to the right of the Tower of Babble and a walk of under five minutes from the road. Most of its dozen routes are bolted sport lines of roughly 70 to 100 feet, with a couple of gear routes and one boulder problem. Difficulty clusters in the 5.11 range, with a lone 5.10 and a few 5.12s, so it suits climbers already comfortable on steep face climbing rather than beginners. Anchors sit below loose terrain, and a helmet is recommended.
